# Explicit count sensitivity — declared before new repetition estimates

The parent plan requires verified timestamps. That requirement is not satisfied and is not relabeled as passed. This separate run implements two conditional analyses of the unresolved pre-buffer record. It produces no certified timestamp repair and no strict-parent primary estimate.

The reviewed diagnostic authenticates the existing June 2023 bullet file and identifies one record with an empty game ID and timestamp zero involving exactly one focal chooser. Its genuine-game status and exact date cannot be established from the available upstream source. The other 321 invalid-time rows do not involve focal choosers. Source bytes and all existing result files remain unchanged.

Scenario A, `valid_timestamp_history`, counts only the time-valid starts in the authenticated chronology. The single reviewed malformed record supplies no prior start. Scenario B, `include_undated_june_record`, conditionally treats that record as one additional June 2023 bullet start, using its archive partition to place it before the October 2023 buffer. The record is not treated as recovered; no point timestamp is supplied. For the affected chooser, the prior same-speed count at every focal bullet opportunity is one greater under B. All other counts agree.

Both interpretations have identical focal observations, accounts, outcomes, sessions, controls, and weighting. A June event cannot bridge into an October session under any of the declared 15/30/60-minute thresholds. Valid recent history and the October buffer determine session positions. Focal tied starts and left-censored sessions retain the parent design's exclusions; no additional focal observation or account is removed for this problem. Initial carries are computed from valid prefix times; including a June record cannot change whether the first October event breaks a session, even if no other prior event is known.

The parent ten repetition specifications are fit under both scenarios, with the parent within-chooser transformation and chooser-clustered covariance. Each scenario reports the original four-test Holm family separately. This does not provide joint eight-test error control, and no scenario is selected by statistical significance. All coefficients, standard errors, intervals and estimability flags are retained. The paired comparison verifies equal row and cluster counts and reports coefficient changes. Two scenario estimates are not mathematical bounds over arbitrary source corruption or all possible hidden histories.

The existing projected focal Parquets and compatible prefix-count checkpoints are reused. Recent history is reconstructed once, and the two scenarios share its Parquets and regression partitions. Unaffected partitions reuse pass-one cross-products. Pass two computes cluster scores at each scenario's own fitted coefficients; covariance is not copied from the other scenario.

No engine runs, API calls, raw-PGN decompression, or receipt/IV/arena reruns are performed. Ordinary-loss and incident-share requirements are not resolved by this package. The separate request to remove the author's accounts is not implemented here; this sensitivity preserves the previously frozen sample and says so in its status.

If additional malformed history involves a focal chooser, the reviewed file changes, or any observation-count check fails, this package stops. It does not generalize the exception to other files. A complete strict-parent result would still require actual recovery of the source record or an explicitly accepted revised history definition.
